title: Loop control request file (.control.json)
description: workspace/memory/.control.json. Single writer = dashboard backend (services/control.py, POST /api/v1/control/pause|resume). Reader = loop control CLI (aidlc.py loop-start/loop-check/wait-resume). Written atomically (temp file in the same directory -> os.replace), UTF-8, no BOM. Any violation of this schema is treated by the CLI as 'control file broken' (exit 2). ADR-004 §1, 20 §5 F4.

schema.description: Contract version. Bumped only on a breaking change.

seq.description: Monotonic request counter. Every write (pause or resume, including idempotent re-writes) sets seq = max(prev, baseline) + 1, where prev = seq of the existing .control.json (0 if missing or broken) and baseline = baseline_seq of loop-status.json (0 if missing or not valid against loop-status.schema.json). Both files are re-read on every write (no in-memory cache) under one in-process lock. This keeps a write after the control file was deleted or corrupted mid-loop above the running loop's baseline_seq, so the CLI applies it (I-16). The CLI compares only seq > baseline_seq and never tracks seq changes, so a re-created file may reuse an earlier seq value. Readers (CLI and dashboard) accept seq only as a JSON integer literal (no bool, no 7.0, no exponent form) within 1..9007199254740991 (2^53-1, JS-safe) - same predicate on both sides; JSON Schema 'integer' alone accepts 7.0, so the extra predicate is mandatory. Otherwise the file is broken. If max(prev, baseline) + 1 would exceed the maximum, the dashboard does not write (500 CONTROL_WRITE_FAILED, existing file kept). loop-cli.md §2.1, §7, ADR-004 Decision 1.1.

state.description: User intent. 'pause' = stop at the next cycle boundary and wait; 'running' = resume / do not pause.

requested_at.description: Time of this write. RFC 3339, timezone-aware UTC, second precision (e.g. 2026-10-23T07:36:23+00:00).

max_pause_sec.description: Maximum length of one pause episode in seconds (measured from loop-status.paused_since). Default 7200. On a resume write the writer keeps the previous value.
